title: The nonnegative-coefficient conjecture for the polynomial h(t,a;r)
statement:
Let $r\in\mathbb N$ and let $h(t,a;r)$ be the polynomial defined in the paper by

$$
h(t,a;r):=[1+(3+a)t]^r\left([1+(2+a)t]^{r+1}-[1+at]^{r+1}\right)-[1+(1+a)t]^r\left([1+(4+a)t]^{r+1}-[1+(2+a)t]^{r+1}\right).
$$

**Nonnegative-coefficient conjecture.** If $r\in\mathbb N$ is arbitrary but fixed, then $h(t,a;r)$, viewed as a polynomial in $(t,a)$, has nonnegative coefficients. This would considerably strengthen the stated inequality $h(t,a;r)\geq0$ for real $a,t\in[0,\infty)$ and $r\in[1,\infty)$.
source_name: James Allen Fill and Svante Janson, “Positive autocorrelation at unit lag for stationary random walk Metropolis-Hastings in R^d”, arXiv:2601.19323 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19323

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

solutions.body:
We prove that the polynomial has nonnegative joint coefficients in \(t\) and \(a\) for every integer \(r\ge0\).

Introduce \(x=1+at\), \(u=t/x\), and
\[
A=(1+3u)(1+2u),\qquad B=(1+u)(1+4u),
\]
\[
C=(1+u)(1+2u),\qquad D=1+3u.
\]
Regrouping the four homogeneous products in the defining polynomial gives
\[
h(t,a;r)=x^{2r+1}g_r(u),
\]
where
\[
g_r(u)=(1+2u)A^r-(1+4u)B^r+(1+2u)C^r-D^r.
\]

The key identity is the following exact positive generating function:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r\ge0}g_r(u)z^r
&=\frac{1+2u}{1-Az}
-\frac{1+4u}{1-Bz}
+\frac{1+2u}{1-Cz}
-\frac1{1-Dz}\\
&=\frac{8u^4z^2(1+2u)}
{(1-Az)(1-Bz)(1-Cz)(1-Dz)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The identity follows simply by taking a common denominator.

Each of \(A,B,C,D\) belongs to \(\mathbb N[u]\). Therefore every factor
\[
\frac1{1-Ez}=\sum_{j\ge0}E(u)^jz^j,
\qquad E\in\{A,B,C,D\},
\]
has nonnegative coefficients in both \(u\) and \(z\). The numerator \(8u^4z^2(1+2u)\) does also. Hence
\[
g_r(u)=\sum_{j=0}^{2r+1}c_{r,j}u^j
\qquad\text{with }c_{r,j}\in\mathbb N
\]
for every \(r\ge0\); the degree bound follows directly from the defining expression for \(g_r\).

Undoing the substitution yields the manifestly positive decomposition
\[
h(t,a;r)
=\sum_{j=0}^{2r+1}c_{r,j}\,t^j(1+at)^{2r+1-j}.
\]
Thus
\[
[t^{j+\ell}a^\ell]h(t,a;r)
=c_{r,j}\binom{2r+1-j}{\ell}\ge0
\]
for all \(j,\ell\). This proves the conjecture for every integer \(r\). In fact \(h(t,a;0)=h(t,a;1)=0\), and for every \(r\ge2\) the polynomial lies in \(8t^4\mathbb N[t,a]\).
